PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY LESSON · PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Airport — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches what an airport is and what happens there — from rolling suitcase to climbing airplane.

What is this?

An airport is where airplanes take off and land, and where travelers check in their suitcases, wait in big bright rooms, and climb aboard.

What does it mean?

Doors to everywhere is the idea: the airport is the town’s biggest door — it opens onto every other place on the map.

What does the child need to know?

You need a suitcase with your name on it, a boarding pass, and shoes that slip off easily — airports ask everyone the same kind steps.

Why this matters

Some family lives too far for a car — a day of driving becomes a few hours of flying, and the whole swap happens in a building with a tower watching the sky.

What it teaches

Sequencing a big trip, name-tag awareness (your suitcase is YOURS), the patience of airport waiting, and the physics show outside the window — planes really do bend up into the sky.

Words to learn

airportairplaneaeroplanesuitcaseboarding passtowertake offlandingwingstrip

Say this to your child

“"The airport! Suitcases roll — brrrrumble — the tower watches the sky, and THERE: the airplane takes off — vrrroooom, up, up and away! One day that will be us, waving at the whole town from the window!"”

Step by step

  1. Roll the suitcase in — wheels singing, name tag facing out.
  2. Check in: the suitcase rides a belt and disappears (do not worry — it meets you at the other end, that is the deal).
  3. Walk the big bright rooms, follow the signs, and look UP — the windows are airplane television.
  4. Watch the tower work: it talks to the planes, and the planes listen — take off means climbing right over your head.
  5. One day soon: your row is called, you walk the tunnel, buckle up, and the town becomes tiny below the window.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the pink airplane climbs right past the control tower — the tower is the airport’s eye, and every take-off happens under its watch.

Ask your child

"Who talks to the airplanes?" (the tower) "Where does the big suitcase go?" (on the belt — it meets us at the other end) "What does the airplane do at take-off?" (climbs — up, up and away)

What your child can say or do

Your child might line up kitchen chairs as an airplane and call rows by number, tag every stuffed animal with a paper name label, or stand at the real airport window calling every landing like an air-traffic announcer.

Out in the real world

It is an airplane to American families and an aeroplane to British families — and either way it leaves from the airport. Many airports have free viewing spots where jets land right over your head; the score-each-landing game is a classic for a reason.

Try it together

Front-row plane spotting: find the viewing spot, score each landing, guess the destination from the colors, and practice the wave — every pilot appreciates it, and one or two flash the lights back.

Understanding check

Ask: "Where do the suitcases go at check-in?" (on the belt — to meet us at the other end) "What watches every take-off?" (the tower)

This lesson pairs with the Airport flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Places in the Community.
